title: The cheap fare is rarely the cheap holiday
subtitle: Two Aegean sailings can look a week apart in price and finish level. Here is where.

text: Compare the disembarkation bill, not the brochure fare.
sub: A fare is only the entry price. The number that matters is what you have paid by the morning you walk off in Piraeus.

title: Three lines that sit outside a low fare

items.head: Drinks, water and coffee
items.body: On mainstream lines this is a package decision made at embarkation. On inclusive fares the decision doesn't exist.

items.head: Gratuities
items.body: Either built into the fare, or added per person per day for the whole voyage. Only one of those is visible upfront.

items.head: Shore excursions and transfers
items.body: The line's own tours, the airport car, the pre-cruise night. Rarely quoted at the same moment as the cabin.

quote: An inclusive fare isn't generosity. It's a line deciding not to sell you anything else once you're aboard.

text: Price the whole week, then choose the ship.
sub: Once both sailings are costed to the same finish line, the decision stops being about money and becomes what it should be - which ship you'd rather spend seven mornings on.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with
body: It's the conversation worth having before either of you falls for a headline fare.
